items.title: The strict nullspace property
items.statement:
Let $m,n\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$, and let
$A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb R)=\mathbb R^{m\times n}$.
Put $[m]:=\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $[n]:=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The library indexes
vector coordinates and matrix columns by $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and matrix rows
by $m=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. Throughout this item use the canonical relabeling
$j\mapsto j-1$ from $[n]$ to the library's coordinate and column indices, and
similarly from $[m]$ for rows. Thus write
$u_j:=u(j-1)$ and $A_{ij}:=A(i-1,j-1)$. For $u\in\mathbb R^n$, define
the matrix-vector product by
$$(Au)_i:=\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}u_j \qquad (i\in[m]),$$
and define
$$\ker A:=\{h\in\mathbb R^n:Ah=0\}.$$
For $h\in\mathbb R^n$ and $S\subseteq[n]$, let $h_S\in\mathbb R^n$ be the
vector whose $j$th coordinate is $h_j$ for $j\in S$ and $0$ for $j\notin S$;
write $S^c:=[n]\setminus S$. For $u\in\mathbb R^n$, write
$$\|u\|_1:=\sum_{j=1}^n|u_j|,$$
the same $p=1$ norm as the library's finite-dimensional norm under this
coordinate relabeling.
For $s\in\mathbb N$ with $1\le s\le n$, the matrix $A$ satisfies the **strict
nullspace property of order $s$** if
$$\|h_S\|_1<\|h_{S^c}\|_1$$
for every nonzero $h\in\ker A$ and every $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le s$.
This condition concerns exact kernel vectors only and says nothing about vectors
with $Ah\ne0$.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.1, Definition 4.1
Afonso S. Bandeira, Ten Lectures and Forty-Two Open Problems in the Mathematics of Data Science, §6.3

items.title: Exact basis-pursuit recovery under the strict nullspace property
items.statement:
Let $m,n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, and let
$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ satisfy the strict nullspace property of order
$s$. Use one-based coordinate labels $j=1,\ldots,n$, with coordinate $j$
identified with the library's coordinate $j-1$. If $x^\dagger\in\mathbb R^n$
has at most $s$ nonzero coordinates, then
$x^\dagger$ is the unique minimizer of
$$\sum_{j=1}^n|z_j|$$
over all $z\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfying $Az=Ax^\dagger$. This is a noiseless
exact-data result; it makes no exact-recovery or support-recovery assertion for
noisy observations.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.1, Theorems 4.4–4.5
Afonso S. Bandeira, Ten Lectures and Forty-Two Open Problems in the Mathematics of Data Science, §6.3

items.title: A uniform stability margin for the nullspace cone
items.statement:
Let $m,n,s\in\mathbb N$ with $m,n\ge1$ and $1\le s\le n$, and let
$A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$. Use one-based coordinate labels
$j=1,\ldots,n$, with coordinate $j$ identified with the library's coordinate
$j-1$. Assume that
$$\sum_{j\in S}|h_j|<\sum_{j\notin S}|h_j|$$
for every nonzero $h\in\mathbb R^n$ with $Ah=0$ and every
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|S|\le s$. Then there is a constant
$\rho\in(0,1)$ such that
$$\sum_{j\in S}|h_j|\le\rho\sum_{j\notin S}|h_j|$$
for every $h\in\mathbb R^n$ with $Ah=0$ and every
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|S|\le s$. The estimate is only on the exact
kernel and gives no bound for vectors with $Ah\ne0$.

references.title: Simon Foucart and Holger Rauhut, A Mathematical Introduction to Compressive Sensing, §4.2, Definition 4.11 and Remark 4.16

title: Sparse recovery and nullspace certificates — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A two-column matrix where basis pursuit is not unique
items.statement:
Let $A=[1\;1]\in M_{1\times2}(\mathbb R)$ and $s=1$, using one-based
coordinate labels $j=1,2$ corresponding to library indices $j-1$. The vector
$h=(1,-1)$ lies in $\ker A$, and for
$S=\{1\}$ the strict nullspace inequality fails because
$\|h_S\|_1=\|h_{S^c}\|_1=1$. Under the constraint $z_1+z_2=1$, the function
$|z_1|+|z_2|$ has minimum $1$, attained both by $x^\dagger=(1,0)$ and by
$z=(0,1)$; therefore the displayed optimization problem has two distinct
minimizers.

items.title: A nontrivial three-column matrix with the nullspace property
items.statement:
Let
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&0\\1&0&1\end{pmatrix}\in M_{2\times3}(\mathbb R)$$
and $s=1$, using one-based coordinate labels $j=1,2,3$ corresponding to
library indices $j-1$. Then $\ker A=\{\lambda(1,1,-1):\lambda\in\mathbb R\}$,
$A$ satisfies the
strict nullspace property of order $1$, and every vector $x^\dagger\in\mathbb
R^3$ with at most one nonzero coordinate is the unique minimizer of
$$\sum_{j=1}^3|z_j|$$
subject to $Az=Ax^\dagger$.

items.title: Identity design: noiseless recovery and a noisy minimax lower bound
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n,d,s\in\mathbb N$ with $n\ge1$, $d\ge2$,
$1\le s\le d/2$, and
$\sigma>0$. Use one-based coordinate labels $j=1,\ldots,d$, with coordinate
$j$ identified with the library's coordinate $j-1$, and put
$$\Theta_{s,d}:=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^d:|\{j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}:\theta_j\ne0\}|\le s\},$$
and let $I_d$ be the $d\times d$ identity matrix. For
$\theta\in\Theta_{s,d}$, observe independent coordinates
$$Y_j\sim N\bigl((I_d\theta)_j,\sigma^2/n\bigr),\qquad 1\le j\le d.$$
The zero kernel of $I_d$ implies the strict nullspace property of order $s$,
so the noiseless basis-pursuit problem uniquely recovers each $s$-sparse
$\theta$. In this noisy Gaussian model, every Borel estimator
$T:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ satisfies
$$\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_{s,d}}\mathbb E_\theta\left[\sum_{j=1}^d(T(Y)_j-\theta_j)^2\right]\ge \frac{\sigma^2s\log(ed/s)}{200000n}.$$
